lawyer:
Abdur Razzak Khan, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Taufique Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellant
Mohammad Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent No. 1
Biswajit Deb Nath, Deputy Attorney General, appeared with the leave of the Court ------ For the Respondent No. 2
parties:
Md. Shahidul Islam ------ Appellant
Vs.
Shepon Bepari and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. This criminal appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 17.05.2005 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 10165 of 2002 under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure discharging the rule and affirming the Judgment and order, dated 12.08.2002 passed by the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Criminal Revision No. 906 of 1999 setting aside the order dated 29.04.1999 passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka in Petition Case No. 3095 of 1998 under Sections 323, 325, 326 and 307 of the Penal Code dismissing the complaint. On a petition of Complaint filed by the present-respondent No. 1 Shepon Bepari the above mentioned petition case No. 3095 of 1998 under sections 323, 325, 326 and 307 of the Penal Code was started. The respondent No. 1 lodged that complaint alleging, inter alia, that he filed Dhanmondi PS. Case No. 40(8)92 against some relatives of this present appellant Md. Shahidul Islam and others. That on 22.07.1996 while the complainant was going across 'Fakirapul Chowrasta' one Motaleb and Amir took him to Motijheel Police Station where the duty officer d. Sahidul Islam (the present appellant), Atique and another named Motaleb assaulted him with roller etc. Hearing that news some of his relative came to the police station for his rescue but the accused-appellant and others demanded Tk. 1,00,000/- (one lac taka) from them as 'Chanda'. They also asked him to withdraw the aforesaid case filed against their relatives. But the complainant refused to do so and the appellant and other accused assaulted him mercilessly. On the following day they released the complainant from the thana hajat and since his condition was serious they got him admitted into Pangu Hospital at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka where he was under treatment for 3 months. Thereafter, the complainant made a complaint to the Home Minister who forwarded the same to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka Metropolitan Police (East) for necessary action, but he took no effective action. The complainant then lodged the complaint to the C.M.M. Dhaka which was registered as petition Case No. 3095 of 1998. 

 2. On receipt of that complaint Mr. Md. Aminul Islam, Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka examined the complainant under section 200 of the Code of Criminal procedure and forwarded the case record to the learned C.M.M. with recommendation for holding a judicial inquiry for ascertaining the truth or otherwise of the allegations. Thereafter, on 18.08.1998 the learned C.M.M. appointed Mr. Abdus Sala, Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka for submitting a report after holding a judicial inquiry into the matter. Accordingly the said metropolitan Magistrate, after holding a judicial inquiry, returned the case record to the learned C.M.M., Dhaka with the inquiry report wherein it was stated that the allegation were found prima facie true on judicial inquiry. 

 3. On receipt of the case record on 14.04.1999 the learned C.M.M. adjourned the hearing on several occasions on different grounds and lastly on 29.7.1999 the learned C.M.M. passed an order dismissing the complaint. On 06.09.1999 the complainant filed a revisional application under section 439A of the Code of Criminal procedure before the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka against the aforesaid order dated 29.07.1999 on the basis of which the Criminal Revision No. 906 of 1998 was stated. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka transferred that criminal revision to the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd court, Dhaka for disposal. The Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, after hearing both the parties, allowed that criminal revision, set aside the order dated 29.07.1999 passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka in petition Case No. 3095 of 1998 and directed the learned Magistrate to proceed with the case in the light of judicial enquiry report. 

 4. Being aggrieved by that judgment and order dated 12.08.2002 passed by the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd court, Dhaka in Criminal Revision No. 906 of 1999 this accused-appellant preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 10165 of 2002 under Section 561A of the Code of criminal Procedure before the High Court Division and obtained rule. Ultimately a Division Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing discharged that rule by the impugned judgment and order upholding the judgment and order dated 12.08.2002 passed by the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Criminal Revision No. 906 of 1999. 

 5. Being aggrieved by this impugned Judgment and order of the High Court Division this accused - appellant preferred Criminal-petition for Leave to Appeal No. 28 of 2006 before this Division. Leave was granted to consider the submissions of the learned Advocate for the leave-petitioner to the effect that the High Court Division failed to consider that the direction given by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka to the C.M.M. to proceed in the light of judicial enquiry report is illegal and without jurisdiction inasmuch as it is, in fact, a direction to the Magistrate to take cognizance of the offence against the petitioner, that on 29.07.1999 the complainant appeared in dock and stated before the learned C.M.M. that he was not willing to proceed with the case and the learned Magistrate recorded his statements and having found no ground to proceed further dismissed the complaint, but the revisional court and the High Court Division failed to consider the legal implication that the contents recorded by the Magistrate are true and that they failed to consider that even a mere statement of the complainant before the Magistrate that he would not proceed with the case was enough to dismiss the complaint by the Magistrate. 

 6. Mr. Abdur Razzak Khan, the learned Senior Advocate, for the accused-appellant has made submissions to the effect that the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd court, Dhaka committed wrong and illegality in setting aside the impugned order dated 29.07.2009 passed by the learned C.M.M. on the finding that the complainant did not file any petition for withdrawal of the complaint ignoring the fact that the said impugned order dated 29.07.1999 proves that the complainant himself stated before the C.M.M. that he not willing to proceed with the case. The learned counsel has argued that the order dated 29.07.1999 clearly shows that the learned C.M.M. heard the complainant himself and the complainant stated before the learned C.M.M. that he wanted to withdraw the complaint against this accused-appellant and another, that the learned C.M.M. himself recorded these facts in the impugned order dated 29.97.1999 and in the circumstances the Additional metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka committed illegality in setting aside the impugned order on the ground that no application was filed by the complainant for withdrawal of the case. The learned counsel has argued also that the judgment and order dated 22.08.2002 passed by the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge directing the learned C.M.M., Dhaka to take cognizance of the offence alleged in the light of recommendations of the inquiry Magistrate was illegal inasmuch as the power to take cognizance is exercisable exclusively by the learned C.M.M. and he cannot be directed by the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge to take cognizance against this accused-appellant and others. The learned counsel has argued that the High Court Division without considering and appreciating legal aspect affirmed the judgment and order of the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd court, Dhaka whimsically and arbitrarily and as such the impugned judgment and order are liable to be set aside. 

 7. Mr. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate-on-record for the complainant respondent No. 1 and Mr. Biswajit Deb Nath, the learned Deputy Attorney General for the state-respondent No. 2 have made submissions supporting the impugned judgment and order. They have made submissions to the effect that the complainant was tortured mercilessly by the accused-appellant and other police officials inside the 'thana' and the complainant was in hospital under treatment for long three months and that these facts were proved prima facie on judicial inquiry and that the complainant had no reason to pray for withdrawal of the complaint, that the very fact that the complainant filed the revision against the impugned order of dismissal of the complaint within a short period strongly tells that actually he did not pray for withdrawal of the case. 

 10. From the above quoted impugned order it is evident that the complainant did not file any application for withdrawal of the case. But it appears that the learned C.M.M. heard the complainant and then made observation to the effect that since the Complainant prayed for withdrawal of the complaint against the main accused 'daroga' Md. Sahhidul Islam and 'daroga' Atique it seemed that the complainant had no allegation against the other accused persons also and the learned C.M.M. then recorded his opinion to the effect that since the complainant was willing to withdraw the case against the principal accused persons there was no justification to keep the case alive against the other sepoys who were subordinates of the principal accused and then passed the order dismissing complaint against all the accused persons. Evidently, this very order dated 29.07.1999 is not proper and justified at all. Even if it is accepted that the complainant wanted to withdraw the case against two of the accused persons then also the dismissal of the entire complaint against all the accused persons was not proper and justified at all. However, it has already been stated above' that within a short period of one month few days the complainant filed the revisional application challenging this very order dated 20.07.1999. It also appears that in this criminal Revision No. 906 of 1999 an application was filed on 20.04.2002 in the name of the complainant praying for withdrawal of the revisional application, but subsequently the complainant also filed an application stating that he did not file that application dated 20.04.2002, that some unknown persons forcibly obtained his signatures on some blank papers and using these signatures filed that application dated 20.04.2002 and prayed for rejection of the application. Considering all these facts and circumstances and also considering the facts that on judicial inquiry the allegations against this accused-appellant and other accused persons were found prima facie true the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions judge, 2nd court, Dhaka allowed the revisional application and set aside the order dated 29.07.1999 passed by the learned C.M.M. dismissing the complainant. The High Court Division also has considered all these facts and circumstances and upheld this order of the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge passed in C.R. No. 906 of 1999. We do not find any infirmity or illegality in the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division affirming those passed by the leaned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd court, Dhaka in Criminal Revision No. 906 of 1999. 

 12. This direction does not mean at all that the learned Magistrate was directed to take cognizance against the accused persons. This direction to the learned Magistrate was to proceed in the light of judicial inquiry report. The learned Magistrate, on consideration of this inquiry report will do what he, in his wisdom, thinks justified. However, the contention of the accused appellant that by the order dated 12.08.2002 passed in criminal Revision No. 906 of 1999 the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions judge directed the Magistrate to take cognizance of the case against the accused persons is not correct at all. 

 13. However, considering the facts and circumstances we do not find that the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd court, Dhaka has committed any wrong or illegality in setting aside the impugned order dated 29.97.1999 passed by the learned C.M.M. Dhaka dismissing the case and as such the High Court Division also did not commit any wrong or illegality in upholding this judgment and order passed in Criminal Revision No. 906 of 1999.
